meta.description: Human-reviewed contributor queue for Morrow. The bot reads this file and nothing else. Every entry is reviewed in a normal pull request: an agent that decides at runtime what to build will duplicate, hallucinate, and file tasks nobody can start. Seeded only with work derived from the actual tree (untested pure modules), not from docs/RESEARCH-AND-ROADMAP.md, which is 38 KB of ideas and belongs here as backlog.
notes: status: backlog -> not eligible to be filed
status: ready   -> eligible; the bot may file it when the cap allows
status: filed   -> bot created it; the marker lives in the issue body
status: shipped -> bot may comment + close its own issue, naming the release
Morrow's constraint: a contributor without Windows must be able to finish any 'easy' item. Do not mark an entry 'ready' if it needs `npm run tauri dev`, the Rust tests, or native dialogs.

items.title: test: cover src/markdown-render.ts, the pure Markdown-to-preview builder
items.body:
## Context

`src/markdown-render.ts` turns Markdown into a bounded, inert preview tree (`buildMarkdownPreview`). It has **no unit test**: `tests/` has `markdown-preview.test.ts` for the panel, but not for the renderer itself. It is the easiest module in the repo to test — one external import (`markdown-it`) and a self-contained contract in `src/markdown-preview-contract.ts` (`MAX_MARKDOWN_CHARS`, `MAX_MARKDOWN_NODES`).

This one runs on **any** OS. You do not need Windows, Rust, or MSVC.

## What to change

- `tests/markdown-render.test.ts` (new): cover the behaviour the limits exist to guarantee.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A document over `MAX_MARKDOWN_CHARS` is truncated, not thrown on
- [ ] A document producing more than `MAX_MARKDOWN_NODES` nodes is bounded, not expanded
- [ ] Raw HTML in the source is rendered as **text**, never as live markup
- [ ] Links and images are disabled in the output tree
- [ ] Uses `vitest` like the neighbouring tests; no new dependency

## How to verify

```bash
npx vitest run tests/markdown-render.test.ts
npm test          # 71 -> more, all green
npm run build
```

## Where to start

1. `src/markdown-render.ts` — 78 lines, read it top to bottom.
2. `tests/markdown-preview.test.ts` — copy its import and assert style.

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours.
items.note: Closed as invalid: src/markdown-render.ts is already covered by tests/markdown-preview.test.ts.

items.title: test: assert the bundled samples stay valid and in sync
items.body:
## Context

`src/samples.ts` holds the `PYTHON_SAMPLE` and `MARKDOWN_SAMPLE` strings shown on first launch — the first thing every new user sees. Nothing tests them, so a broken fence or a stray tab becomes a visible bug in the product's first impression.

**Blocked on a decision, not on work.** The obvious criterion — "balanced code fences in `MARKDOWN_SAMPLE`" — cannot be written: that string contains **no** code fences today. Asserting an even count of a thing that does not appear is a test that passes for the wrong reason and would block anyone who later adds a fence-bearing sample. Choose one, then move this back to `ready`:

1. Assert what is actually true now: both exports are non-empty, `PYTHON_SAMPLE` has no tab indentation and ends with a newline, and the two samples differ.
2. Add a code fence to `MARKDOWN_SAMPLE` first (a product change), then assert balance.

Runs on any OS.

## What to change

- `tests/samples.test.ts` (new), depending on which option above is chosen.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both exports are non-empty strings
- [ ] `PYTHON_SAMPLE` contains no tab indentation and ends with a newline
- [ ] The two samples are not identical
- [ ] Fence handling matches whichever decision is recorded on this issue

## How to verify

```bash
npx vitest run tests/samples.test.ts
npm test
```

## Where to start

1. `src/samples.ts` — 54 lines, two exports.
2. `tests/encoding.test.ts` — the simplest existing test file to copy the style from.

## Time estimate

~1 hour once the question above is answered.

items.title: test: extend encoding coverage to BOMs, mixed line endings and round-trips
items.body:
## Context

`src/encoding.ts` does `decodeFile` / `encodeFile` / `inspectLineEndings` over raw `Uint8Array`, and it is where "my file got mangled" bugs come from. `tests/encoding.test.ts` has 15 passing tests — this issue extends it rather than starting it, so you are working from examples.

Runs on any OS.

## What to change

- `tests/encoding.test.ts`: add cases for the three edges below.

## Acceptance criteria

Three of the five edges originally listed here are **already covered**, so they are not repeated:
BOM round-tripping (4 encodings × 3 line endings), CRLF byte-for-byte survival, `mixed: true`,
and invalid bytes throwing a clear error all have tests today.

- [ ] A file of exactly `MAX_FILE_BYTES` is accepted by `decodeFile`, and one byte over is refused with the 20 MiB message
- [ ] The same limit on the write path: `encodeFile` output at exactly `MAX_FILE_BYTES` succeeds, one byte over is refused
- [ ] A UTF-32 LE file (starts `ff fe 00 00`) is refused with the "UTF-32 is not supported" message rather than decoded as UTF-16 LE. `decodeFile` special-cases this; nothing tests it
- [ ] Each new case follows the existing file's style: bare `it(...)`, no new dependency, no snapshot

## How to verify

```bash
npx vitest run tests/encoding.test.ts
npm test
npm run build
```

## Where to start

1. `src/encoding.ts` — 102 lines, four exports. `MAX_FILE_BYTES` is line 4, the UTF-32 check is around line 34.
2. `tests/encoding.test.ts` — 15 existing tests show the fixture style; the "rejects invalid bytes…" case is the closest model for the refusal tests.

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours. Note the 20 MiB fixtures: build the boundary case with a length assertion rather than allocating 20 MiB twice if you can.

items.title: docs: add CONTRIBUTING.md with a Windows-free development path
items.body:
## Context

GitHub's community profile reports `contributing: MISSING` for this repo (`health_percentage: 42`), and the README's Contributing section is four lines. `SECURITY.md` is also absent, which matters because `src/arena.ts` takes an API key. The bigger problem: nothing tells a visitor that most of Morrow is platform-neutral TypeScript they can work on without Windows or MSVC.

## What to change

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` (new) covering: the Windows-free path (`npm ci`, `npm test`, `npm run test:e2e`), what genuinely requires Windows (`npm run tauri dev`, `cargo test`, native dialogs), commit style, and the reply SLA.
- `SECURITY.md` (private disclosure via GitHub Security Advisories; no bounty).
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml`, `config.yml`, `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Linux/macOS contributor can follow it to a green `npm test`
- [ ] It names what cannot be done off Windows rather than implying Windows is required for everything
- [ ] `community/profile` health reaches 100 and reports a security policy

## How to verify

```bash
npm ci && npm test
curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/RANJITHROSAN17/morrow-editor/community/profile | grep health_percentage
```

## Where to start

1. `README.md` §"Development and testing" — the commands already exist there.
2. `.github/workflows/windows.yml` — shows the full gate CI runs.

## Time estimate

~1 hour.

items.title: chore(ci): publish the built installer as a tagged preview release
items.body:
## Context

`windows.yml` already builds the NSIS installer and writes `SHA256SUMS.txt`, then uploads them as an artifact that expires, and there are **0 releases and 0 tags**. The installer already has a checksum but no permanent home.

## What to change

- `.github/workflows/windows.yml`: on a `v*` tag, create a release with the `.exe` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` attached.
- Release notes must lead with the README's existing honesty line: early preview, unsigned, keep backups.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A tag push produces a release with both assets
- [ ] The asset downloads without a GitHub login
- [ ] The release body says "unsigned preview", not "production"
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` moves 0.4.0 from "unreleased preview" to a dated heading

## How to verify

```bash
git tag v0.4.0 && git push origin v0.4.0
gh release view v0.4.0
```

## Where to start

1. `.github/workflows/windows.yml` — the build, checksum and upload steps already exist.
2. `CHANGELOG.md` — the release text is already written.

## Time estimate

~1-2 hours.
